title: What If Every Seagrass Meadow Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every seagrass meadow vanished? A tiny slice of ocean holds a huge amount of carbon.
Seagrass covers a sliver of the sea, yet it buries over 10 percent of the ocean's carbon each year.
Per square kilometer, it can hold up to 83,000 tonnes of carbon, against about 30,000 for a typical forest.
About 90 percent sits in the soil, locked away for decades to centuries.
Destroy the meadows and some of it escapes. Estimates say up to 25 percent as much as land deforestation.
And roughly 29 percent are already gone, with at least 1.5 percent of the rest lost every year.
